test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: By selling cloth at ₹483/m, a shopkeeper loses 31%. Find the rate (in /m) at which it should be sold so as to earn a profit of 34%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 31% means selling at **(100 − 31) = 69%** of CP.

Profit of 34% means selling at **(100 + 34) = 134%** of CP.

Ratio-unitary method: If 69 units = 483, then 1 unit = 483 ÷ 69 = 7.

Target Selling Price = 134 units = 134 × 7 = 938.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹938/m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = ₹483, Loss% = 31%, Target Profit% = 34%.

**Formulas:** CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%], New SP = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b10c750b5b865d1e69a8a97c55e2402a25959d185f7f153494bcff1176b48851.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = (483 × 100) ÷ (100 − 31) = (483 × 100) ÷ 69 = 7 × 100 = ₹700.

⇒ **Required Selling Price (SP₂)** = [700 × (100 + 34)] ÷ 100 = 700 × 1.34 = 938.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹938/m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When the cost price is constant, the ratio of two selling prices is directly proportional to the percentage values: **SP₁/SP₂ = (100 ± P/L₁)/(100 ± P/L₂)**.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit is earned when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when CP > SP. All percentages are calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.
